LESSON: SIGN READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: POEMS AND STORIES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poems and Stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poems and Stories, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we read the title and pictures in a story? 2. Why should we discuss through signing pictures in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Poems and Stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner confidently identifies and talks about events in a story logically and fluently.

● Learning to learn: learner uses appropriate sign reading techniques to answer questions appropriately.

Values:
Responsibility: Determination as learner engages in assigned roles and duties diligently.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to link the concept of reading poems and songs to their learning in Kiswahili.
